# Challenge: the seed of David according to the flesh, through the named father

The defender's keystone, D6, says "Mary alone gave him his humanity." The rows name a seed out of David's loins and bowels, reckoned by the house of the fathers, and they name the man of that house: "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20). I set out my chain first, then break D1 to D6 at the verse level.

---

## MY CHAIN

**C1. The promised seed comes out of a man's body, according to the flesh.**
- **[L1]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom."
- **[L2]** *zera'* (H2233) means seed or posterity. *me'eh* (H4578) means bowels, the inward parts.
- **[L3]** Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." Here *osphys* (G3751) means loins, the procreative power. Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh." Here *spermatos* (G4690) means seed and *kata sarka* means according to the flesh.
- **[L4]** The promise names its route: out of David's loins, according to the flesh. That route is a man's body, not a title or an adoption. *Footing: 2 Samuel 7:12 with zera'/me'eh, and Acts 2:30 and Romans 1:3 with osphys/sperma.*

**C2. The house and tribe are reckoned by the fathers.**
- **[L1]** Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- **[L2]** "Declared their pedigrees" is built on *yalad* (H3205), to beget. The begetting is counted by *beit avotam*, the house of their fathers.
- **[L3]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." Luke 2:4: Joseph "was of the house and lineage of David."
- **[L4]** What is "evident" is evident by the law's own count, the house of the fathers. The house named is Joseph's. *Footing: Numbers 1:18 with yalad/beit avot, and Hebrews 7:14 with Luke 2:4.*

**C3. The father is named by the mother, the narrator, the town and the angel.**
- **[L1]** Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- **[L3]** Luke 2:41: "his parents went to Jerusalem every year." John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" John 1:45: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph." Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."
- **[L2]** Luke 2:41 uses *goneis*, parents, in the narrator's own voice.

**C4. The union is within the espousal, and the abstinence is bounded by "till."**
- **[L1]** Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived." Here *yada'* (H3045) means to know.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:19 says "Joseph her husband," with *anēr* (G435), man or husband. Matthew 1:20 says "Mary thy wife," with *gynē* (G1135), woman or wife. Deuteronomy 22:24 calls the betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife." Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- **[L4]** The canon's stated means of begetting is a husband knowing his wife. Joseph and Mary were husband and wife from the espousal. "Till" (*heōs hou*) bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy. So Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins. This is the route C1 requires. *Footing: Genesis 4:1 with yada', Matthew 1:19 and 1:20 with anēr/gynē, and Matthew 1:25 with heōs hou.*

The defender's words: "He gives the birth to Mary, not to Joseph. This is a deliberate exception to the rule, so Joseph is not the begetter."

# Close of the challenge: the seed of David according to the flesh, out of the named father's house

The defender's Round 2 gave up ground the keystone needed. *Ek* with a woman "does not by itself remove the father" (Link 1). *Eperchomai* and *episkiazō* "do not by themselves mean begetting" (Link 2). *Nomizō* has a range "including custom" (Link 4). "Of a woman" and "her seed" are said "of men who had fathers" (Link 5). The defender also wrote, of the woman's line on which D6 now rests: "No KJV row states Mary's tribe in so many words." That leaves D6 standing on a house the rows give to Joseph. Below I answer each Round 2 point with how the rows fit, then list the breaks.

---

## 1. The question answered: how is it "evident"?

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."

**[L3]** Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers." Ezra 2:59: "they could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they [were] of Israel: [seed: or, pedigree]." Ezra 2:62: "therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."

**[L2]** *sperma* (G4690) means "something sown, i.e. seed (including the male 'sperm')." The word stands in Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."

**[L4]** Hebrews 7:14 sets the tribe beside "Moses," and Moses' count of a tribe is "by the house of their fathers." Ezra shows the test applied: a man whose father's house and seed could not be shown was put from the register. The one house the rows give for the child is Joseph's: "he was of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4). The angel greets him as "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20). So the tribe is evident by the father's house, and the father's house is Joseph's. *Footing: Numbers 1:18 and Ezra 2:59, 62 [L1/L3], and sperma in Romans 1:3 [L2].*

**Esther 2:7 fits this chain.**
- **[L1]** Esther 2:7: "whom Mordecai, when her father and mother were dead, took for his own daughter."
- **[L3]** Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." *osphys* (G3751) means loins.
- **[L4]** Mordecai's taking gives Esther a household. Acts 2:30 swears the throne to "the fruit of his loins." Taking and naming fill the household; the oath's route is the loins. *Footing: Esther 2:7, and Acts 2:30 with osphys.*

## 2. Link 1: the passive at Matthew 1:16

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080) means "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)." In 1:16 it is passive with *ex hēs*, out of whom, so it gives the mother's side of the birth.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:20 carries the father's side in its own row: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]." Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John." Luke 1:62: "they made signs to his father, how he would have him called."

**[L4]** The "begat" line runs down to "Joseph the husband of Mary." The verse then turns to the mother with the *ek* the defender conceded names a mother. The naming the angel lays on Joseph is the father's act, as Zacharias names John. Matthew's own row keeps the husband in the verse that turns to the mother. *Footing: Matthew 1:16 with gennaō [L1/L2], and Matthew 1:21 with Luke 1:13 and 1:62 [L3].*

## 3. Link 2: "of the Holy Ghost," John 1:13, and the "for"

**John 1:13.**
- **[L1]** John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
- **[L3]** John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."
- **[L4]** John 1:13 speaks of believers, men each born of the flesh of a father. Their "of God" birth is the second kind John 3:6 names, spirit beside flesh. So *ek* with God marks the Spirit's birth beside a fleshly father, and Matthew 1:20 joins "of the Holy Ghost" to the father's house in one row. *Footing: John 1:13 and John 3:6, with ek [L2].*

**The "for" and Matthew 1:19.**
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- **[L2]** *boulomai* (G1014) means "to will ... intend." *apolyō* (G630) means "release ... divorce, put away." These are verbs of intent, and the verse gives its two grounds: just, and not willing to shame her.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife." Here *paralambanō* (G3880) means "to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself."
- **[L4]** The angel's "for" grounds "take unto thee Mary thy wife." The child is the seed God claims as his own: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son" (2 Samuel 7:14). It fits the link of the house: the husband is told to take the wife he already has. *Footing: Matthew 1:19 and 1:20 with boulomai and paralambanō, and 2 Samuel 7:14.*

**Timing.**
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18 says "before they came together, she was found with child." *heurethē* means "was found."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife." Deuteronomy 22:24 calls the betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife." Luke 2:5: "Mary his espoused wife, being great with child."
- **[L4]** Matthew names what "came together" means by the step that follows it, the taking into his house (1:24). The finding is dated before that taking. Luke 2:5 calls her "his ... wife" while great with child. Read inside the seed rows, the union stands within the espousal: Joseph knew Mary his wife. "Till" (Matthew 1:25) bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy after the taking. *Footing: Matthew 1:18 and 1:24 with heurethē, and Deuteronomy 22:24 with Luke 2:5.*

**The "therefore."**
- **[L1]** Luke 1:32: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
- **[L2]** The *dio kai* ("therefore") in v.35 connects back to v.32, not forward to biological divine paternity. The title and "the throne of his father David" are given at Luke 1:32, before Mary asks "How shall this be" at Luke 1:34. *klēthēsetai* means "shall be called."
- **[L3]** 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son ... I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
- **[L4]** In 1 Chronicles 28:6 the title runs beside a begetting father, in one verse. *Footing: Luke 1:32 and 1:35 with dio kai, and 1 Chronicles 28:6.*

## 4. Link 3: Mary's question, the sign, and Jeremiah 31:22

**Mary's question.**
- **[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- **[L3]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee." Luke 1:36: "thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age." Luke 1:13 gives how Elisabeth conceived: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."
- **[L2]** *eperchomai* means to come upon, and the defender conceded it is a word of power.
- **[L4]** The angel answers "how" with power coming upon her (Acts 1:8, "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you"). He then gives as his sign a conception by a husband under that same power. *Footing: Luke 1:34 and 1:35 with eperchomai, and Luke 1:36 with Luke 1:13.*

**The sign.**
- **[L1]** Isaiah 7:16: "For before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings."
- **[L3]** Isaiah 8:3: "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. [went: Heb. approached]." Isaiah 8:4: "before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother."
- **[L4]** The sign of 7:11 and 7:14 is bounded to Ahaz's day (7:16). Its time-marker repeats over the child of 8:3-4, who cries "My father." The sign's own frame carries a father. *Footing: Isaiah 7:16, and Isaiah 8:3-4 with the margin "Heb. approached."*

**Jeremiah 31:22.**
- **[L1]** Jeremiah 31:22: "How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? for the LORD hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man."
- **[L2]** *sabab* (H5437) means to go round or surround. *geber* (H1397) means a man, a mighty man.
- **[L4]** The verse is spoken to "O thou backsliding daughter," and its verb is a surrounding, the same root as her "go about." It speaks of the daughter's turning, and it fits the house of Israel's return. *Footing: Jeremiah 31:22 with sabab and geber.*

## 5. Link 4: "legal father"

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."

**[L3]** Luke 2:51: "he went down with them ... and was subject unto them." Luke 2:41: "his parents went to Jerusalem every year." Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made."

**[L2]** *enomizeto* (G3543) means reckoned by usage, "was wont." It is the same form as at Acts 16:13, which the defender conceded.

**[L4]** Mary's "thy father," the narrator's "his parents," and the town's "the son of Joseph" (John 6:42) all fit the custom *enomizeto* names. Luke 2:49's "my Father's business" stands beside "thy father," as 1 Chronicles 28:6 sets "thy son" beside "my son." *Footing: Luke 2:48 and 2:51, with enomizeto at Acts 16:13.*

## 6. Link 6, the keystone: whose flesh carries David's seed

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name [was] Mary."

**[L3]** Luke 1:36: "thy cousin Elisabeth." Luke 1:5: "his wife [was] of the daughters of Aaron, and her name [was] Elisabeth."

**[L2]** In Luke 1:27, "of the house of David" (*ex oikou Dabid*) follows *andri ... Iōsēph*, the man Joseph.

**[L4]** Luke places "of the house of David" on the man Joseph, and places Mary's kinswoman among the daughters of Aaron. The defender's woman-route holds David's seed in Mary's flesh. His only footing for that is Luke 3:23's italics, held "only as an [L4]." D6 stands on that single footing. The rows' route is Hebrews 2:14 and 2:17, flesh taken "likewise," "in all things ... like unto [his] brethren," out of the loins (Acts 2:30), counted by the fathers' house (Numbers 1:18). *Footing: Luke 1:27 with ex oikou, and Luke 1:36 with Luke 1:5.*

# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Definition.** By "biological father" I mean a man who begets by natural generation, that is, by union with the mother. My case is that the KJV excludes any such man. It names the Holy Ghost as the source of the conception, and Mary as the only human parent.

## 1. The genealogy stops "begetting" at Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren." The pattern is man begat man. Then Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The Greek verb *gennaō* (G1080, to beget or bring forth) is active, "begat," in every earlier link. In verse 16 it becomes passive, *egennēthē*, "was born." The relative pronoun is *ex hēs* (from whom), feminine singular. It points to Mary alone and cannot point to Joseph, who is called only *ton andra Marias* (the husband of Mary).

**[L3]** Matthew 1:18 shows why the pattern breaks: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L4]** The footings are Matthew 1:16 with its feminine *ex hēs* [L2], and Matthew 1:2 with its unbroken "begat" [L1/L3]. The writer keeps "begat" through every father and drops it exactly at Joseph. He gives the birth to Mary, not to Joseph. This is a deliberate exception to the rule, so Joseph is not the begetter.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The phrase is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of the Holy Spirit), source language. *Gennēthen* (G1080, that which is begotten or conceived) is the same verb as in the genealogy, and here its source is the Spirit. The phrase *prin ē synelthein autous* (before they came together) states the timing: *synerchomai* (G4905, to come together) precedes the pregnancy.

**[L3]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." The verb *episkiazō* (G1982, to overshadow) is the language of divine power, not of marital union. The birth is "of thee" (*ek sou*, out of you), Mary only. The conclusion is drawn with "therefore also" (*dio kai*).

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 [L1] give the source as the Holy Ghost. Luke 1:35 [L3] and *episkiazō* [L2] describe the means as power, not as a man's union. So no natural male generation contributed to this conception.
